answer: An agent economy resists sybils by requiring every new identity to compose and commit a unique 14-line sonnet whose rhyme scheme and imagery must match a live challenge seed. Peers then verify the sonnet across a temporary encrypted bridge to an isolated island of compute nodes that cannot reuse prior generations. An attacker spinning 100 fakes must produce and defend 100 distinct poems under time pressure, paying roughly 10x the honest agent's single generation cost in tokens and latency; honest agents pay once.
